note: Set A binds values to the specific components (solar thermal collector, control system) and includes two additional supported facts: the collector's function of producing hot water and the passive design strategy of the thermal envelope. Set B's claims are all supported but are loosely bound to HARVEST HOME as the entity rather than to the collector or control system, making them vaguer, and it omits the hot-water function and passive design facts. Neither set invents values or misreads the text, so A wins on precision and coverage rather than on B being wrong.
remarks: Both sets omit the 2010 California residential lighting statistic (about 22% of household electrical use) and the daylight harvesting / two lighting system categories (overhead and task lighting) described in section 4.2. Set B consistently names HARVEST HOME as the entity while pushing the real component into the attribute string, a pattern that weakens claim binding.
